title: Cocomplete preaisles contain transfinite extensions of complexes
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$. Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category with $\mathcal V$-small Hom sets and all colimits indexed by $\mathcal V$-small categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be the unbounded derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal V_0$ be a strictly full subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$ containing zero and closed under $\mathcal V$-small coproducts, $[1]$, and extensions: the middle object of a distinguished triangle belongs to $\mathcal V_0$ whenever both end objects do. Let $\theta$ be a $\mathcal V$-small ordinal and $(E_\beta^\bullet)_{\beta\leq\theta}$ an ordinal-indexed diagram of complexes, with $E_0^\bullet=0$, all transition maps degreewise monomorphisms, and $E_\lambda^\bullet=\varinjlim_{\beta<\lambda}E_\beta^\bullet$ degreewise at every nonzero limit $\lambda\leq\theta$. If $Q(E_{\beta+1}^\bullet/E_\beta^\bullet)\in\mathcal V_0$ for every $\beta<\theta$, then $Q(E_\theta^\bullet)\in\mathcal V_0$. No boundedness, compactness, or direct-summand closure hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Step 2, middle t-structure existence input. Agent-formulated auxiliary transfinite-closure lemma for the set-generated-aisle proof; this assertion is not proved in the blueprint. WANTED: a general reference proving that cocomplete preaisles in Grothendieck derived categories are closed under filtered homotopy colimits/transfinite extensions. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Induct on $\beta\leq\theta$, with induction assertion $Q(E_\beta^\bullet)\in\mathcal V_0$. The base case is $E_0^\bullet=0$. At a successor, degreewise monicity gives $0\to E_\beta^\bullet\to E_{\beta+1}^\bullet\to E_{\beta+1}^\bullet/E_\beta^\bullet\to0$. Apply the short-exact-sequence triangle theorem. Its first and third objects lie in $\mathcal V_0$, respectively by induction and the successive-quotient hypothesis. Extension closure puts the middle object $Q(E_{\beta+1}^\bullet)$ in $\mathcal V_0$.

source.place: Step 2, middle t-structure existence input; agent-supplied transfinite induction, base and successor.

proof.text: Let $\lambda\leq\theta$ be a nonzero limit ordinal and assume the induction assertion below $\lambda$. The $\mathcal V$-small preorder $I=\{\beta:\beta<\lambda\}$ is nonempty and filtered: the maximum of two indices is still below $\lambda$, and there are no distinct parallel arrows. Its colimits in $\mathcal A$ are exact by the Grothendieck hypothesis. For $D(\beta)=E_\beta^\bullet$, form the bar total $B^\bullet$ of [def-sc-preorder-bar-total]. Its $p$th column $B_p^\bullet$ is the coproduct of $E_{\beta_0}^\bullet$ over $\beta_0\leq\cdots\leq\beta_p<\lambda$, and the total degree is $q-p$. Each finite-string index set is $\mathcal V$-small. The derived-coproduct theorem and the induction hypothesis give $Q(B_p^\bullet)\in\mathcal V_0$. Continuity identifies the degreewise colimit of $D$ with $E_\lambda^\bullet$. The exact-colimit bar-augmentation theorem therefore gives a quasi-isomorphism $B^\bullet\to E_\lambda^\bullet$, including for unbounded complexes.

source.place: Step 2, middle t-structure existence input; agent-supplied ordinal bar construction at a limit.

proof.text: For $n\geq0$ let $T_n^\bullet$ retain columns $0\leq p\leq n$ of $B^\bullet$. The horizontal face differential lowers $p$, while the vertical differential retains $p$, so these columns form a subcomplex. The inclusion $T_n^\bullet\to T_{n+1}^\bullet$ is degreewise the inclusion of a finite partial sum. In its quotient only column $n+1$ remains; its vertical differential is $(-1)^{n+1}d$, so the quotient is precisely $B_{n+1}^\bullet[n+1]$ with the stated shift convention. Thus $T_0^\bullet=B_0^\bullet$ and the short-exact-sequence triangle for $0\to T_n^\bullet\to T_{n+1}^\bullet\to B_{n+1}^\bullet[n+1]\to0$ proves $Q(T_n^\bullet)\in\mathcal V_0$ by ordinary induction: the quotient belongs by step 2 and repeated closure under $[1]$, and extension closure gives the middle object. The column calculation is a direct computation from the bar total, not a boundedness assumption.

source.place: Step 2, middle t-structure existence input; agent-supplied finite horizontal skeleta.

proof.text: Put $W^\bullet=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}T_n^\bullet$, write $j_n:T_n^\bullet\to T_{n+1}^\bullet$ for inclusion, and define $u\iota_n=\iota_n-\iota_{n+1}j_n$. Let $q:W^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ sum the skeletal inclusions. In each degree, $B^r=\bigoplus_{p\geq0}B_p^{r+p}$ is the colimit of its finite partial sums $T_n^r$: compatible maps from the partial sums are exactly families of maps from all the summands. A morphism $h:W^r\to X$ satisfies $hu^r=0$ exactly when its components satisfy $h_n=h_{n+1}j_n^r$. These compatible components factor uniquely through $B^r$, so $q^r$ is a cokernel of $u^r$. The general sequential-telescope monomorphism lemma makes $u^r$ monic. Its hypothesis holds because exact filtered colimits in a Grothendieck abelian category preserve finite limits, including kernels and finite biproducts; the indexing categories here are countable or categories of finite subsets of $\mathbf N$, hence $\mathcal V$-small. Consequently $0\to W^\bullet\xrightarrow{u}W^\bullet\xrightarrow{q}B^\bullet\to0$ is degreewise short exact. This proves the telescope exactness directly in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Tag 093W, lemma-compute-colimit; direct cokernel universal-property argument for the skeletal sequence.

proof.text: By the derived-coproduct theorem, $Q(W^\bullet)$ is a coproduct of the $Q(T_n^\bullet)$, so step 3 and coproduct closure put it in $\mathcal V_0$. Apply the short-exact-sequence triangle theorem to step 4 and rotate the distinguished triangle once, obtaining $Q(W^\bullet)\to Q(B^\bullet)\to Q(W^\bullet)[1]\to Q(W^\bullet)[1]$. The first and third objects belong to $\mathcal V_0$, using $[1]$-closure for the third. Extension closure now gives $Q(B^\bullet)\in\mathcal V_0$. Rotation is essential here: the unrotated triangle has $Q(B^\bullet)$ as its third object.

source.place: Step 2, middle t-structure existence input; agent-supplied passage from finite skeleta to the full bar total.

proof.text: The quasi-isomorphism $B^\bullet\to E_\lambda^\bullet$ from step 2 is inverted by the derived localization. Strict fullness therefore transfers membership from $Q(B^\bullet)$ to $Q(E_\lambda^\bullet)$. This completes the limit step and hence transfinite induction through $\theta$. The argument only used nonnegative shifts, extensions, and the stated small coproducts; it did not require boundedness, compactness, or closure under direct summands.

Its generic abelian-derived triangle applies to successor quotients and the two skeletal short exact sequences.

Its universal property is used to identify the skeletal union and the telescope cokernel.
